identity: A 1922 Arabic magazine profile (ترجمة حياته) of Amin Fares al-Rihani, the Lebanese-American writer, written on the occasion of his visit to Egypt. Two movements: an ornate nahda-style panegyric in rhymed enumerative prose (paragraphs 1-4), then a plain chronological biography (paragraph 5). Register = §V, original-Arabic nahda essay.
law: §V has dense stops. In the biographical narrative the productive unit is the EPISODE, ~10-16 tokens: و + finite verb opening a new phase of the life CUTS (وتعلم, وهاجر, وطالع, وتولد, ومكث, وخطب, واشتد, وكتب, ونظم, وطبع, وعاش), and so do fronted temporals (ولما, وبعد طبعها, وفي عام ١٩٠٤, وبعد إقامته) and أما topic-fronting (أما معيشته, أما صفاته, أما الآن). What welds: ف as the immediate consequence of the clause before it (فشغف, فدخل, فأعجب, فمال, فقبلتها, فأقام), a second verb that is the same beat as the first (وجال معها, ومكث في قرية الفريكة, ونشر المقالات, ووضع على رأسه, ونفع بهم), و joining nouns in the long epithet and noun chains, asyndetic relatives on an indefinite (كان في أثنائها, نشرها أكثر الجرائد, حرك فيها, خطب فيها), locative حيث, and the trailing لأنه / التي / لما clauses.
reasoning: The hard part is paragraph 1 and paragraph 2, which are single ornate periods in the sajʿ manner. Paragraph 1 hangs on ما ذكر اسم الأمين إلا وتمثل ... كاتب, where كاتب @33 is the delayed subject, so nothing before @43 can cut; after that the text becomes a run of asyndetic predications about him (تعرب أشعاره @44, the bare epithets أفرنجي الأسلوب @61, يبتكر @69, ينظم @81) and I cut at each - @43 @60 @68 @80 - on the ground that these were commas or stops in the source and 86 tokens cannot be one segment. @68 is my weakest: the epithets أفرنجي الأسلوب عصري الأفكار could equally be fronted modifiers of يبتكر, so lo. Paragraph 2 I deliberately left WHOLE at 67 tokens: ومن اطلع ... ومن سمع ... is a two-part fronted subject whose predicate is يعجب @132, and cutting anywhere would sever subject from predicate; the second ومن is و + relative pronoun, a coordinate constituent, not a new clause. Same for paragraph 3, held whole by إن كاتبا ... خليق @182. In the biography I applied one consistent test - new episode versus second beat - which is why وجال معها @306 and ومكث @475 weld while وتعلم @244 and وطبع @499 cut. @368 فسافر I welded into فأشار عليه الطبيب rather than leaving a 4-token segment, on the same consequence rule that welds the other seven ف's. The closing character sketch reverts to epithet runs (مقر بضعفه ... بشوش الوجه, ربع القامة ... عريض الجبهة) which I keep whole as comma-lists per LAW 3, cutting only at the أما hinges and the asyndetic verbs جمع, لا يقيد, يعشق, كان منذ سنوات. 49 boundaries over 710 real tokens = 14.5 per segment, inside the band.
